summary: A feature dated October 15, 2023 on fall farm-to-table salads and homemade dressings. It profiles local chefs, bloggers and critics who share dressing ideas, ingredient pairings and plating tips, and it recommends sourcing produce from farmers' markets and CSAs. Seasonal stars include apples, beets, pomegranates and persimmons, and the note stresses balancing flavors and matching dressings to greens.
one_line: An October 2023 feature on autumn farm-to-table salads, covering seasonal ingredients, homemade dressings, green pairings and Instagram-ready plating from local food personalities.
key_facts: The article is dated October 15, 2023 and celebrates fall produce such as root vegetables, sturdy greens and late summer fruits.
Oliver Hudson of Thyme and Season Farmhouse Eatery in Springfield hosted his first Fall Flavors Workshop on September 28, 2023, teaching DIY dressings.
Oliver Hudson suggests autumn dressings built on apple cider vinegars, spiced pecans and roasted squash emulsifications.
The Springfield Farmers Market runs every Saturday from September through November and offers crisp apples, heirloom carrots and chard.
Hannah Rodriguez, a food blogger, shared her 'Golden Autumn Dressing' on September 22, 2023, made with roasted garlic, Dijon mustard, local honey and cider vinegar.
Sullivan James became locally famous at the Harvest Feast on October 3rd for his Maple-Tahini Drizzle, which includes a note of cardamom.
Jasmine Yu, a food critic, hosted the 'Greens and Mean Dressings' workshop at the Arbor Café on September 30, 2023, stressing that a powerful dressing can overwhelm a tender green.
Delicate mache or butter lettuce pairs with a gentle shallot vinaigrette, while peppery arugula pairs with a fig-based dressing.
Food writer Leo Grant's September 15 column promoted pomegranates and persimmons as this year's 'it' ingredients for salads.
Elise and Thomas Carter run the meal prep service 'Simply Seasonal' and were roasting pears and making balsamic reductions in late September 2023.
Nikita Fowler unveiled her 'Fall Salad Series' on Instagram on October 10, 2023, and advises that 'Your followers eat with their eyes first.'
